SYNTHETIC CONTRACT FAMILY - CONTOSO / ADATUM SERVICES

1. Master Services Agreement (Jan. 1, 2025): 2-year term; liability cap $500,000; Delaware law; 90-day convenience termination for Customer; order of precedence: MSA, then SOWs; amendments must be in signed writing referencing the MSA.

2. SOW #1 (Feb. 1, 2025): Managed analytics services; $40,000/month; term coterminous with MSA.

3. Amendment No. 1 (July 1, 2025): Liability cap changed to fees paid in prior 12 months (approx. $480,000).

4. Data Processing Addendum (Aug. 15, 2025): 24-hour incident notice; EU SCCs attached; prevails over MSA for data-protection conflicts.

5. Renewal Letter (Jan. 1, 2027): Extends MSA through Dec. 31, 2027; all other terms unchanged.

6. Side Letter (Mar. 1, 2027): Customer may terminate on 45 days' notice; prevails over inconsistent MSA terms. Signed by Adatum VP Sales (not an authorized signatory under MSA Section 18.3).

7. Amended and Restated MSA (July 1, 2027): 18-month term; cap $750,000; New York law; entire-agreement clause supersedes "all prior agreements regarding its subject matter"; expressly preserves the DPA and SOW #1; silent on the Side Letter and Amendment No. 1.

8. SOW #2 (Sept. 1, 2027): AI forecasting services under the Restated MSA; includes its own 6-month cap of $200,000 for SOW #2 claims.

Contract-family renewal readinessBefore a complex, amended contract family renews or a new instrument is added to it, confirm what currently governs, how its terms compare to the portfolio standard, what is operationally due, and whether any related draft is ready to sign.
Outcome: One combined renewal-readiness packet: relationship map, comparison grid, obligations tracker, and execution-readiness checklist, each citing its own source clause.
Negotiation turn reviewWhen a negotiation turn arrives from the other side, confirm it still reflects what was commercially agreed, understand what changed and who benefits, and run the mechanical checks before it goes back out.
Outcome: One negotiation-turn packet: deviation report, redline summary, defined-term defects, and cross-reference issues.
Precedent-to-signature draftingTurn a set of approved precedents into reusable standards, draft a new agreement from one of them, review the draft against the new playbook, and confirm it is ready to sign.
Outcome: One drafting-to-signature packet: the derived playbook, the new draft, the playbook-review findings, and the execution-readiness check.
Matter update and counsel memoBuild a reliable factual record for an active dispute, roll it into a portfolio-level update for leadership, and turn one contested question from that update into a counsel-ready memo.
Outcome: One escalation packet: case chronology, matter status update, and a memo answering the one legal question that update surfaced.

Legal Skills in Word vs. Legal Plugin in Cowork

Both surfaces draw from the same 21-skill catalog: 18 skills work in both, 1 is Word only, and 2 are Cowork only. Use this matrix to decide where to start, then use the Word or Cowork tab to try it.

Choose Word when...

  • One legal document is already open and is the center of the task
  • You need native tracked changes you can accept or reject in place
  • The work is included in your Microsoft 365 Copilot license with no extra usage cost

Choose Cowork when...

  • The task spans several documents, emails, or a matter's full context
  • You need a standalone report, tracker, or multi-stage workflow output
  • You are comfortable with usage-based Copilot Credit consumption

All 21 skills

Hover, focus, or select any skill to see what it does and where it is available.

  • Draft new contractTell Copilot to generate new draft contracts based on templates or previous contracts.
    Use case: Accelerate first-draft creation while retaining approved structure and style.
  • Edit contractTell Copilot what to change and it produces negotiation-ready redlines with tracked changes across relevant sections, minimizing unnecessary edits and preserving original formatting.
    Use case: Convert a negotiation instruction into precise language without rewriting unrelated terms.
  • Create playbookCreate a playbook from a set of precedents.
    Use case: Convert institutional knowledge in executed agreements into repeatable review positions.
  • Review contractReviews contracts against playbooks, addressing conflicts and recommending edits to align with internal standards and approved language.
    Use case: Deliver consistent, repeatable contract review across negotiators.
  • Summarize redlinesExplain each tracked change, its impact, and who benefits.
    Use case: Give decision-makers a fast negotiation update without line-by-line review.
  • Compare key termsCreate a comparison of terms across documents.
    Use case: Give negotiators and leadership a side-by-side view of key terms across a contract portfolio.
  • Analyze related contractsIdentify how contracts interact and which terms remain in force.
    Use case: Resolve which document and version governs today.
  • Check execution readinessIdentify issues that may need to be addressed before signing a legal document.
    Use case: Reduce avoidable signature-package defects without giving legal sign-off.
  • Check cross-referencesFind broken or unclear cross-references and suggest fixes.
    Use case: Prevent execution errors caused by renumbering and missing attachments.
  • Compare against agreed termsHighlight deviations from agreed commercial terms.
    Use case: Verify negotiated commercial terms were implemented correctly.
  • Check defined termsFind issues with defined terms and suggest fixes.
    Use case: Catch defined-term defects before signature or before they are copied forward into a new precedent.
  • Extract obligations and deadlinesCreate a tracker of obligations and key dates.
    Use case: Convert dense contract language into an operational checklist.
  • Identify regulatory gapsHighlight potential gaps against applicable legal or policy requirements.
    Use case: Create a traceable compliance-gap inventory instead of a general risk summary.
  • Legal reasoningAnalyzes full agreements, drills into specific clauses, and compares versions to spot risks and obligations, with citations linking to source language.
    Use case: Quickly identify rights, obligations, notice periods, ambiguities, and practical implications.
  • Explain legal conceptsMake complex legal language easier to understand without losing important details.
    Use case: Help non-lawyers understand what a deal requires and how to operate within it.
  • Draft legal memoCreate a structured legal memo.
    Use case: Turn a defined legal-document question and record into structured counsel analysis.
  • Compare across jurisdictionsCreate a side-by-side analysis across jurisdictions.
    Use case: Give counsel a structured starting point before advising on a multi-state or multi-country question, without being mistaken for a jurisdiction-specific opinion.
  • Summarize legal mattersSurface key developments, actions, deadlines, and open questions.
    Use case: Give legal leadership a concise portfolio update.
  • Build case chronologyTurn case materials into a dated timeline.
    Use case: Create a reliable timeline for strategy, witness preparation, pleadings, and hearings.
  • Draft minutes and resolutionsCreate formal records of decisions and actions from a meeting transcript.
    Use case: Produce a consistent record of attendance, discussions, recusals, decisions, and actions.
  • Improve legal promptGet help writing clear and effective prompts.
    Use case: Turn vague instructions into scoped prompts with sources, perspective, issues, output, and constraints.

📖 Legal terms glossary

Plain-language definitions for the legal terms used across this demo, with the skills where each one applies.

Redline
A tracked-changes markup showing proposed insertions and deletions to a document's text, so reviewers can see exactly what changed.
Edit contractReview contractSummarize redlines
Playbook
A company's written set of preferred and fallback contract positions, used as the standard a draft is measured against.
Create playbookReview contract
Liability cap
A contractual ceiling on how much one party can be required to pay the other in damages, usually tied to fees paid.
Edit contractReview contractCompare key termsAnalyze related contracts
Carve-out
An exception that removes certain claims (such as confidentiality or IP infringement) from a general limit like a liability cap.
Edit contractReview contract
Indemnity
A promise by one party to cover the other party's losses arising from specified claims, such as third-party lawsuits.
Review contractCompare key termsCompare against agreed terms
Convenience termination
The right to end a contract for any reason (not just a breach), usually after a notice period and sometimes with an early-termination fee.
Review contractLegal reasoningCompare key terms
Cure period
A window of time a breaching party is given to fix a problem before the other party can terminate for that breach.
Legal reasoningBuild case chronology
Novation / Amendment
A novation substitutes a new party into a contract; an amendment changes specific terms of an existing agreement without replacing it.
Analyze related contracts
Side letter
A separate signed document that modifies or adds to a main agreement, which may or may not have been properly authorized.
Analyze related contracts
Entire agreement clause
A clause stating the written contract is the complete deal, which can supersede earlier agreements on the same subject.
Analyze related contracts
Escrow
Funds held by a neutral third party (often to cover post-closing claims) and released after a set period if no claim is made.
Compare against agreed terms
Basket
A deductible-style threshold of losses that must be reached before a party can claim against an indemnity.
Compare against agreed terms
Chronic failure
Repeated service-level failures over time that can trigger a termination right, beyond a single missed SLA.
Review contractCompare key terms
SLA (Service Level Agreement)
A commitment to a measurable standard of service, such as percentage uptime, with consequences if it is not met.
Review contractCompare key terms
Deemed acceptance / Deemed approval
A contract mechanic where silence within a stated window counts as agreement, shifting the burden to act onto the recipient.
Extract obligations and deadlines
Defined term
A capitalized word or phrase given a specific meaning in a contract, which should be used consistently throughout.
Check defined terms
Cross-reference
A pointer from one part of a document to another section, schedule, or exhibit, which can break when a document is renumbered.
Check cross-references
Governing law
The jurisdiction's law that will be used to interpret and enforce the contract, regardless of where the parties are located.
Compare key termsReview contractCompare across jurisdictions
Assignment
The transfer of a party's rights or obligations under a contract to another entity, often restricted without consent.
Compare key termsReview contract
Non-compete
A restriction preventing a person from working for a competing business for a defined period after employment ends.
Compare across jurisdictions
Recusal
A person voluntarily stepping away from a decision due to a conflict of interest, so they do not vote or participate in it.
Draft minutes and resolutions
Quorum
The minimum number of members who must be present for a governing body's meeting and votes to be valid.
Draft minutes and resolutions
DPA (Data Processing Addendum)
A contract attachment governing how a service provider handles personal data on a customer's behalf.
Analyze related contractsExtract obligations and deadlines
SOC 2
An independent audit report on a service provider's security, availability, and confidentiality controls.
Create playbookReview contractExtract obligations and deadlines
Operative term
The version of a contract term that currently governs, after accounting for every amendment, restatement, or related instrument.
Analyze related contracts
